title: Restore American Samoa and Wallis–Futuna Natural Earth boundary source profiles
body:
Bounded source-policy and semantic follow-up from #134.

The published baseline has five American Samoa IDs (`ASM-4998` Eastern, `ASM-4999` Manu's, `ASM-5000` Rose Atoll, `ASM-5001` Swain's Island, `ASM-5002` Western) and three Wallis and Futuna IDs (`WLF-4995` Sigave, `WLF-4996` 'Uvea, `WLF-4997` Alo). The parent issue explicitly records missing original source-policy profiles for source key `natural-earth`. The present review cannot establish source release/vintage, tier role, license beyond Natural Earth's public-domain product statement, complete district/island coverage, or dry-land/lagoon/boundary semantics from that fallback alone. Its GSHHG comparison is diagnostic and not evidence of administrative borders.

Recover pinned original Natural Earth objects and official local/territorial statistical or legal sources for these exact eight units. Assess every assigned unit, province wrapper, subordinate district/settlement inventory, detached islands and source vintage/license. Distinguish the customary kingdoms and census divisions from legal/current administration and from physical island land. Make no unilateral boundary, hierarchy, ownership, grid, schema or live-data edits. Output source-level recommendations with exact reproducible citations or explicit unresolved findings; coordinate any inter-region issue if primary sources put the units in conflict with a neighboring published grouping.

Dependency: finish and merge #134 first. This follow-up is blocked for scope/source review and cannot be claimed meanwhile.

Checked all 258 open ready geography items across three search pages; no overlapping owned-path prefix was found. Completed parent reservations for reused directories are released, with handoff notices on those parent issues. Marked `status:ready` at the user's request; the moderator takes no reservation. Original evidence must remain preserved. Workers must acquire the normal serialized reservation. This enables evidence research/corrections only, with no regional approval, historical imports or shared/live geography edits.
